clue.text: Jack's terribly thin-drink ?

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman), so Jack's gives AB plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of thin are badly mangled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor complains that his drink has been watered down far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor's nickname, as is AB, an able seaman; the possessive supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Damsel in distress and City lawyer in Us

parts.note: Rome is the Eternal City
a DA is a District Attorney, a prosecutor in the United States

explanation.surface: A maiden in trouble is helped by a city lawyer working in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is the OCR's reading of 'U S'. A DA is an American district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda in Greek myth was chained to a rock as a sea-monster's prey until Perseus rescued her.

clue.text: They include a terrible liar about love aboard

indicators.note: include tells us the letters for aboard hold everything else

parts.note: a ship is an SS (steamship), and aboard means within it

indicators.note: about tells us the anagram is placed round the letter for love
terrible tells us the letters of liar are badly mangled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: A crew contains a dreadful fibber who boasts of love on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is only an article; 'terrible' rearranges just LIAR. 'aboard' points to SS, the steamship whose crew the opening pronoun stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafarers are the people meant by the clue's opening pronoun, which the rest of the clue describes.

clue.text: Nickel, first one in Germany, so it is

definitions.text: Nickel, first one in Germany, so it is

parts.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
erst is German for first
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A list of things found in Germany, beginning with nickel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Germany' makes both 'first' and 'one' German words; 'so it is' confirms the whole thing is in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Nierstein is a Rhineland town famous for its white wine.

clue.text: Male artist illustrates Hebe's mother

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A man paints a picture of a goddess's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: An RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hera, Zeus's wife, bore Hebe, goddess of youth.

clue.text: Diminutive pound-no return for the City

parts.note: something diminutive is tiny, like a baby
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: a return is a going back, so the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: A tiny sum of money, not repaid, is all the City of London offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NO into ON. 'the City' here is the ancient city on the Euphrates, not London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the great ancient Mesopotamian capital, often called simply the great city.

clue.text: Creatures about to yearn for possessions

indicators.note: about tells us the word for creatures goes round the word for yearn

parts.note: beings are creatures
to long for something is to yearn for it

explanation.surface: Animals longing for property of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to yearn' looks like the verb governing 'for possessions', but 'for' is only the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Belongings are personal effects, the things one owns.

clue.text: American loafer embraces, for instance, an Eastern princess

indicators.note: embraces tells us the word for the loafer hugs the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: bum is American slang for an idle vagrant
eg (exempli gratia) means for instance

explanation.surface: A lazy American hugs an oriental princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loafer' is not a shoe but an idler; BUM is American slang for a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A begum is a Muslim noblewoman or high-ranking lady of South Asia.

clue.text: She knocks it back twice in the meadow

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed pair goes inside the word for meadow

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, in poetry

indicators.note: twice tells us the word it appears two times
back tells us the doubled word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A woman drinks it down twice while out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks it back' looks like drinking, but 'back' only turns IT to TI, which 'twice' repeats inside LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a girl's name, so it can stand for any woman referred to by a pronoun.

clue.text: Refusal of the French to make crossings

parts.note: no is a refusal
des is French for of the, plural

explanation.surface: French people refuse to build road junctions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodes are points where lines or branches intersect.

clue.text: Take your car right into a low haunt

indicators.note: into tells us the letter for right goes inside the word for a low haunt

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drive straight into a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor somewhere in your own vehicle is to steer it along the road yourself.

clue.text: Banished bankrupt ambassador

clue.text: Boost one odd player

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange about the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A single strange item is meant to give a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges BOOST plus I into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist performs on the oboe, so is a musician in an orchestra.

clue.text: Enlivens Miss Oakley, we hear-and chums

indicators.note: we hear tells us the name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Annie Oakley was the American sharpshooter of Wild West shows
chums are friends, or mates

explanation.surface: A famous sharpshooter livens things up together with her friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie Oakley, the Wild West markswoman, gives ANNIE, said aloud as the opening sound ANI.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate something is to bring it to life or make it lively.

clue.text: Publisher's first annual list omits nothing for Sa sportsmen

indicators.note: omits tells us a letter is dropped from the publisher's list

parts.note: a publisher's first list of the year is the spring books
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A publisher's catalogue leaves out the South African rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'SA', South Africa; the Springboks are its national rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: Springboks is the nickname of South Africa's national rugby players.

clue.text: She's back in East Island

indicators.note: back here tells us the words East Island are read in reverse

parts.note: an isle is an island

explanation.surface: A woman has returned home to an island off the east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns E plus ISLE into the girl's name. The 's is the verb 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, so it can stand for any woman referred to by a pronoun.

clue.text: Plait once formed into decorative material

indicators.note: formed into tells us the letters are shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A braid is being worked into ornamental fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges the letters of PLAIT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Point lace is needle-made lace, a fine ornamental fabric.

clue.text: Will finds old Bob lacking spirit under canvas

indicators.note: under canvas means inside a tent, so the pieces go within the word for canvas

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, abbreviated s
tame means meek or lacking spirit

explanation.surface: An old man named Bob, too timid to venture out, writes his will while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s. 'under' puts S plus TAME inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Theatrical backer in vice rumpus, according to the Gospel

indicators.note: in tells us the backer goes inside the rearranged word
a rumpus is a commotion, so the letters of vice are thrown into disorder

parts.note: an angel is someone who finances a stage production

explanation.surface: A theatre investor is caught up in a vice scandal, Gospel-style.
explanation.walkthrough: An angel is theatre slang for a financial backer; 'rumpus' scrambles VICE to EVIC around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic means relating to the teaching of the Christian Gospels.

clue.text: Plentiful, like twelve lords at Christmas?

definitions.meaning: in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, the lords are a-leaping, that is jumping about

explanation.surface: A carol's twelve leaping lords are plentiful at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' there are 'ten lords a-leaping'; leaping is bounding, so the lords are 'a-bounding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means present in large numbers, and to be a-leaping is to be jumping in bounds.

clue.text: Be too much like Belloc's Matilda — take top bunk:

definitions.text: Be too much like Belloc's Matilda
definitions.meaning: in Hilaire Belloc's cautionary verse, Matilda told dreadful lies, so being too much like her is telling untruths to excess
to rest stretched out above something else

explanation.surface: Someone who fibs too much grabs the upper bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc's 'Matilda, Who told Lies, and was Burned to Death' is a comic cautionary poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The two senses are to fib excessively and to be stretched on top of something.

clue.text: Country seen in glossy Rialto prints

indicators.note: seen in tells us the answer can be spotted inside the following words

explanation.surface: A nation appears in shiny pictures of the Venice bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across glosSY RIAlto; 'prints' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation of the Middle East.

clue.text: Bluster disconcerts Tories? Right

indicators.note: disconcerts means throws into confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Blustering talk upsets the Conservatives, who lean to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerts' rearranges TORIES to ROISTE; the Tories are Britain's Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily and swagger boisterously.

clue.text: Divinity they love to record inwardly

indicators.note: inwardly tells us the other pieces go inside the word they

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O
to log something is to record it

explanation.surface: Couples love to keep a private diary of their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they love to record' reads as a sentence, but 'inwardly' splits THEY to take O plus LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Divinity is the academic study of religion, as taught in seminaries.

clue.text: The Head requests that they be performed

definitions.text: The Head requests that they be performed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A head teacher asks that certain jobs be done.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: jobs a head asks to be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are jobs or duties that someone is set to carry out.

clue.text: After a breather, East makes a thrust

indicators.note: after tells us the letter for East follows the word for a breather

parts.note: a lung is an organ for breathing

explanation.surface: After pausing for breath, a fencer from the East makes a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward attack, as in fencing.

clue.text: Counterfeiting soccer star

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, governing soccer in England
a king is a leading figure, a star in his field

explanation.surface: A famous footballer is caught forging money.
explanation.definitionFit: Faking means forging or making a fraudulent copy of something.

clue.text: Vessels of our navy in America

indicators.note: in tells us the navy's letters go inside those for America

parts.note: US is the United States of America
RN is the Royal Navy, the British navy

explanation.surface: British warships are stationed in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our navy' for a British paper is the Royal Navy, RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, such as those for ashes.

clue.text: "The falls on castle walls " (Tennyson.)

parts.note: a missing word from the opening line of Tennyson's song from The Princess, The Bugle Song, about glorious light falling on the castle walls

explanation.surface: A line of Tennyson's poetry with its key word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash where the missing word goes; the OCR has lost it. The line opens Tennyson's 'Bugle Song' in The Princess.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Tennyson used means magnificence or brilliant glory of light.

clue.text: Something cast back after former praise

indicators.note: after tells us the reversed piece is placed following the word for former

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: back tells us the letters of the word for something cast are reversed

parts.note: a lot is cast when drawing lots

explanation.surface: An object thrown back comes after earlier acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LOT to TOL; a lot is what you cast when drawing lots.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or celebrate someone highly.

clue.text: Could they buy female elks perhaps?

definitions.text: Could they buy female elks perhaps?

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may form some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether money could buy lady elks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition, since shekels are money that could buy things; 'perhaps' rearranges ELKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shekels are coins, ancient and modern Israeli currency, slang for money in general.

clue.text: Like Juvenal the cat, Irish- Manx perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written, the word cat

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so Irish loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A tailless Irish cat from the Isle of Man resembles a Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' cuts the tail from IRISH to leave IRIS; 'perhaps' rearranges CAT and IRIS. The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, has no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal was a Roman poet famous for his biting satires.
